previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding was admitted for melena, fatigue, and lightheadedness. Initial evaluation revealed anemia with hemoglobin dropping to 7.5 g/dL and acute kidney injury likely due to prerenal causes from poor intake and blood loss. She underwent EGD and colonoscopy, both showing no active bleeding, with EGD revealing non-bleeding esophageal varices. Capsule endoscopy showed no evidence of small bowel bleeding. Renal function improved with IV fluids and albumin, and diuretics were safely restarted. Hemoglobin stabilized at 8.5 g/dL without transfusion. She was discharged home with plans for specialist evaluation, weekly CBC monitoring, and continuation of GI and liver-protective medications.

baseline) on admission. Previous admission with ___ to 1.4 that 
resolved back to baseline with albumin.  Likely prerenal as 
patient presented has been having increased stool output with 
lactulose and conitnued oozing of blood via GI tract. Less 
concern for hepatorenal syndrome. No signs of infection, no

increased bowel movements with lactulose vs ongoing slow GI 
bleed. No localizing infectious etiology. No tapppable pocket.

came down to baseline 9 by discharge. Cirrhosis complicated by
